rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Prophets may mistake a liar for a truthful person before revelation; they remain human and judge by what they hear.
rows.anchor: ينكر أن يعتقد الأنبياء عليهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet believed ʿAbd Allah b. Ubayy and disbelieved Zayd b. Arqam about the latter's report until revelation disclosed the truth.
rows.anchor: قد صدق عليه السلام عبد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Joseph's brothers used sophistry and argument; their case did not compel Yaʿqub to obstinate denial.
rows.anchor: فكلام اخوة يوسف إنما هو مغالطة ومحاجة لا إلزام عناد

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وغيره
rows.claim: They killed a young sheep or kid, stained Joseph's shirt, and showed it to Jacob; he found no tear or tooth mark and inferred their lie.
rows.anchor: قص هذا القصص ابن عباس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jacob challenged them that a wolf could not eat Joseph while leaving his shirt un-torn; this was his circumstantial proof.
rows.anchor: متى كان الذئب حليما، يأكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Malik's legal school used this episode to support acting on circumstantial signs in matters such as the oath of group liability (qasama).
rows.anchor: واستند الفقهاء إلى هذا في

rows.speaker: الشافعي
rows.claim: The shirt held three signs: it exposed their lie, testified by its tear, and later restored Jacob's sight.
rows.anchor: قال الشافعي: كان في القميص ثلاث آيات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another report says the brothers smeared a wolf's mouth with blood; Jacob summoned it, and it crouched and spoke to deny their story.
rows.anchor: وروي أنهم ذهبوا فأخذوا ذئبا فلطخوا فاه بالدم وساقوه وقالوا ليعقوب

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari takes kadhib as either blood associated with a lie or blood falsely accused; he cites a poetic analogy with maʿqūl.
rows.anchor: هذا كلام الطبري، ولا شاهد له فيه عندي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author rejects al-Tabari's evidence and reads kadhib as a verbal noun used adjectivally for emphasis.
rows.anchor: وإنما «الدم الكذب» عندي وصف بالمصدر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads the word with an unpointed dāl, giving the sense of fresh blood or similar; the author considers this reading weak.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن: «بدم كذب» بدال غير معجمة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawwalat means that the souls made the matter pleasing and desired: they had contrived an ugly deed against Joseph.
rows.anchor: بل سولت لكم أنفسكم أمرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The nominative fa-sabrun jamīl can be parsed with an omitted subject, meaning my affair is beautiful patience, or an omitted predicate, meaning beautiful patience is better.
rows.anchor: فصبر جميل رفع إما على حذف الابتداء وإما على حذف الخبر

rows.speaker: الأشهب وعيسى بن عمر
rows.claim: They read fa-ṣabran jamīlan in the accusative with an implied verb; the same reading is reported in the codices of Ubayy and Anas.
rows.anchor: وذكر أن الأشهب وعيسى بن

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh regards the accusative reading as weak, since this construction is suitable only with an imperative; the author says it works if Jacob turns to address himself.
rows.anchor: وهي قراءة ضعيفة عند سيبويه ولا يصلح النصب في مثل هذا إلا مع الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Poetic lines illustrate the imperative accusative and a nominative reading construed as addressing a camel; the accusative here can be saved by Jacob speaking to himself.
rows.anchor: وإنما تصح قراءة النصب على أن تقدر يعقوب عليه السلام رجع إلى مخاطبة نفسه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beautiful patience means not voicing one's complaint to another human; a Prophetic report says the one who broadcasts hardship has not shown beautiful patience.
rows.anchor: وجميل الصبر ألا تقع شكوى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Saying God is the source of help expresses submission to God's decree and reliance on Him to bear what the brothers describe.
rows.anchor: والله المستعان على ما تصفون

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿIbād is the plural of ʿabd; God uses the honorific form here, unlike the form ʿabīd.
rows.anchor: «العباد» جمع عبد، وعرفه في التكرمة

rows.speaker: فرقة من النحويين
rows.claim: One grammatical view makes yuqīmū jussive through an elided imperative lām; Sibawayh says this omission is allowed only in poetry, as in the cited line.
rows.anchor: قالت فرقة من النحويين: جزمه بإضمار لام الأمر

rows.speaker: أبو علي وغيره
rows.claim: Another view treats the present verb as built in the imperative's meaning, by analogy with an indeclinable vocative noun.
rows.anchor: أبو علي وغيره- هو فعل مضارع بني

rows.speaker: سيبويه
rows.claim: Sibawayh parses the verb as the answer to an implied condition: if you tell them to pray, they will pray.
rows.anchor: وقال سيبويه: هو جواب شرط مقدر يتضمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author also allows it as the response to the command qul, understood as convey the law; alternatively the words to be conveyed may be the next verse about God the Creator.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يكون جواب الأمر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say the conveyed words are the following verse, beginning with God who created the heavens and earth.
rows.anchor: وقيل إن المقول هو: الآية التي بعد، أعني قوله:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Secret giving means voluntary alms and public giving obligatory alms, as the hadith evidence implies; Ibn ʿAbbas glosses the verse generally as alms and the prayer as the five prayers, which the author sees as an audience-friendly approximation.
rows.anchor: صدقة التنفل، و «العلانية» المفروضة- وهذا هو مقتضى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Khilāl is the verbal noun of mutual affection; al-Akhfash instead calls it a plural of khulla, and Imruʾ al-Qays supplies a poetic usage.
rows.anchor: وخلال مصدر من خالل: إذا واد وصافى

rows.speaker: نافع وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers use nominative bayʿ and khilāl, treating lā as cancelled; Abu ʿAmr, al-Hasan, and Ibn Kathir use the accusative with lā of absolute negation.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وعاصم وحمزة والكسائي

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو والحسن وابن كثير
rows.claim: These readers put bayʿ and khilāl in the accusative under lā of absolute negation; the passage identifies the day as the Resurrection.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو والحسن وابن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage recalls God's blessings and power, showing His beneficence to humanity and establishing the proof from two sides.
rows.anchor: الآية، تذكير بآلاء الله، وتنبيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In the sentence, Allah is the subject and alladhī is its predicate; inward acceptance of this statement should lead a person to faith, prayer, and almsgiving.
rows.anchor: والله مبتدأ، والذي خبره. ومن أخبر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The heavens are the seven celestial levels, while the sky from which water descends in 2:22 means the clouds.
rows.anchor: والسماوات هي الأرقعة السبعة والسماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Min in min al-thamarāt may be partitive, excluding harmful or barren produce, or explanatory of the kind; calling it extra is rejected by Sibawayh but allowed by al-Akhfash.
rows.anchor: وقوله: من الثمرات يجوز أن تكون من للتبعيض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some grammarians call min extra: Sibawayh disallows this in an affirmative clause, while al-Akhfash permits it.
rows.anchor: وقال بعض الناس: من زائدة- وهذا لا يجوز

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fulk is a plural of fulk; bi-amrihi is an infinitive of God's command, meaning created things take the form He says they should take, including the ships' motion.
rows.anchor: والفلك جمع فلك- وقد تقدم القول فيه مرارا-

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The subjection of ships entails the subjection of the sea and winds; rivers are made to flow through lands and serve irrigation and other benefits.
rows.anchor: وفي «تسخير الفلك» ينطوي تسخير البحر وتسخير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dāʾibayn means continuously; the Prophet used the related verb of a camel kept continually at work, while the verse's apparent sense is the sun and moon's regular courses and benefits.
rows.anchor: ودائبين معناه: متماديين ومنه قول النبي

rows.speaker: مقاتل بن حيان عن ابن عباس
rows.claim: He explains dāʾibayn as the sun and moon continually obeying God; the author accepts this as submission through subjection, or as devotional obedience if that is intended.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن مقاتل بن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gifts are addressed to humankind collectively: every kind of useful thing that people could ask for has been given, though blessings are distributed among individuals.
rows.anchor: وقوله: وآتاكم للجنس من البشر، أي إن الإنسان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An alternate paraphrase says God gave people everything they would have asked for if they had asked.
rows.anchor: وقيل المعنى: وآتاكم من كل ما سألتموه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author says the alternative reading of God's gifts is close to his preceding collective interpretation.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا قريب من الأول

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In mā saʾaltumūhu, mā can be a verbal noun with the pronoun referring to God, or a relative pronoun with the pronoun referring to what was given.
rows.anchor: وما في قوله: ما سألتموه يصح أن تكون مصدرية

rows.speaker: الضحاك بن مزاحم والحسن وقتادة وسلام
rows.claim: They read kull with tanwīn, as is also reported from Nāfiʿ; the gifts then refer to useful things among the created things previously named.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك بن مزاحم «من كل ما سألتموه»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that reading, mā is the second object of ātākum; some instead take it as negative, a construal the passage attributes to al-Dahhak.
rows.anchor: ف ما في قوله: ما سألتموه مفعول ثان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the first reading, where kull is annexed to mā, a second object must be supplied, such as a part or thing.
rows.anchor: وأما القراءة الأولى بإضافة كل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's blessings are too numerous to count, including senses, capacities, creation after nonexistence, and guidance to faith.
rows.anchor: لكثرتها وعظمها في الحواس والقوى والإيجاد بعد العدم والهداية للإيمان وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: طلق بن حبيب
rows.claim: God's due is too weighty for servants to fulfill and His blessings too many to enumerate, so people should end morning and evening repentant.
rows.anchor: وقال طلق بن حبيب: إن حق الله تعالى أثقل

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Whoever sees God's blessings only in food and drink has little knowledge and faces punishment.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء: من لم ير نعمة الله عليه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-insān means the human kind, in which injustice and ingratitude appear in different forms: one in a denier and another in a sinful believer.
rows.anchor: وقوله: إن الإنسان يريد به النوع والجنس المعنى:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The description first concerns Arab disbelievers who rejected resurrection; ḥabiṭat means their deeds became void, including whatever good they had done.
rows.anchor: وهذه صفة المخاطبين من كفار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One literal reading is that no good deeds remain to place on their scales; a person with no good deeds must be in Hell.
rows.anchor: يحتمل أن يريد أنه لا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Alternatively, the weighing language is metaphorical and means they have no standing or worth with God.
rows.anchor: ويحتمل أن يريد المجاز والاستعارة

rows.speaker: أبو هريرة
rows.claim: Abu Hurayra reports the Prophet's comparison of a gluttonous, long-bodied man who weighs less than a mosquito, after which he recited this verse.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو هريرة عن النبي

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص
rows.claim: Saʿd identifies the people who lose their worldly effort while thinking it good as worshippers among Jews and Christians, including monks and hermits.
rows.anchor: فقال سعد بن أبي وقاص

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: Ali identifies the group as the Khawarij; a report says he told Ibn al-Kawwa that he and his companions were the greatest losers.
rows.anchor: وقال علي بن أبي طالب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author weakens these sectarian identifications because the following verses describe people who disbelieved in the meeting with God, unlike Jews, Christians, or Khawarij as groups.
rows.anchor: ويضعف هذا كله قوله تعالى بعد ذلك أولئك الذين كفروا بآيات ربهم ولقائه وليس من هذه الطوائف من يكفر بلقاء الله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He takes the passage as describing polytheistic idol-worshippers; Saʿd and Ali may have named only groups exemplifying part of the opening description.
rows.anchor: فاتجه بهذا ما قلناه أولا وعلي وسعد رضي الله عنهما ذكرا أقواما أخذوا بحظهم من صدر الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aʿmālan is accusative as a specification (tamyīz).
rows.anchor: وقوله أعمالا نصب على التمييز

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وأبو السمال
rows.claim: They read fa-ḥabiṭat with fatḥa on the bāʾ, whereas the majority use kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «فحبطت» بكسر الباء، وقرأ ابن عباس

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Mujahid reads fa-lā yuqīm with yāʾ, meaning God does not set up their weight; the majority use the first-person plural nūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ كعب بن عجرة والحسن وأبو عمرو ونافع والناس «فلا نقيم لهم» بنون العظمة،

rows.speaker: عبيد بن عمير
rows.claim: He reads fa-lā yaqūm, making the weighing a nominative subject; Mujahid also reports a yāʾ reading of yaqūlu lahum.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عبيد بن عمير: «فلا يقوم» ويلزمه أن يقرأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Dhālika points to the abandonment of weighing; their recompense is the predicate, with Hell as an appositive, while mā in bimā kafarū is verbal and huzʾ means mockery.
rows.anchor: وقوله ذلك إشارة إلى ترك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening question prompts the listener to attend, like beginning an account of something surprising by asking whether the listener knows it.
rows.anchor: هذا الاستفهام هو توقيف مضمنه تنبيه النفس إلى استماع ما يورد عليها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verb governing id is implicit in ḥadīth, roughly asking what Moses did when he saw the fire.
rows.anchor: العامل في إذ ما تضمنه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage answers disbelievers' blasphemous claims about Mary and related matters, declaring God above what false speakers say.
rows.anchor: ظاهر هذه الآية الرد على من قال من الكفار أمر مريم وما ضارعه من الكفر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Lahw here means a woman; a report says that in some Arab dialects it means a wife.
rows.anchor: «اللهو» في هذه الآية المرأة وروي أنها في بعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: In in kunna fāʿilīn may be conditional, meaning if We were doing so, though We are not; others take it as a negation, and theologians debate the options.
rows.anchor: وأن في قوله إن كنا فاعلين يحتمل أن تكون الشرطية بمعنى لو كنا أي ولسنا كذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥaqq includes the Qurʾan, the message, the law, and all truth; al-bāṭil likewise covers falsehood generally.
rows.anchor: «الحق» عام في القرآن والرسالة والشرع وكل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yadmughuhu means to strike the brain, a fatal blow in humans; likewise truth destroys falsehood.
rows.anchor: ويدمغه معناه يصيب دماغه وذلك مهلك في البشر فكذلك الحق يهلك الباطل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wayl can mean disgrace and grief or the name of a valley in Hell, which is the intended sense if the latter view is adopted.
rows.anchor: والويل الخزي والهم وقيل هو اسم واد في جهنم فهو المراد في هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning addresses disbelievers who ascribed to God what is improper and unfitting.
rows.anchor: وهذه مخاطبة للكفار الذين وصفوا الله تعالى بما لا يجوز عليه ولا يليق به

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: He says the codices of Ibn Masʿud, Ubayy, and Hafsa add that Shuʿayb was their brother; the passage explains this as human and prophetic kinship, not blood relation.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش في مصحف ابن

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وابن عامر
rows.claim: These readers say aṣḥāb Layka here and in Ṣād, while other readers have al-Ayka; Ayka denotes a dense tree grove, or a known lush tree favored by doves.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وابن كثير وابن

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada says the grove consisted of doum palms.
rows.anchor: وقال قتادة كان شجرهم هذا دوما

rows.speaker: أبو عبيد القاسم بن سلام
rows.claim: Some commentators cited by Abu ʿUbayd take Layka as the town's name; another group treats it as an eased pronunciation of al-Ayka.
rows.anchor: «ليكة» اسم البلد في قراءة ذلك قاله بعض المفسرين

rows.speaker: أبو علي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli says the missing alif in the codex does not privilege the Layka pronunciation, since spelling follows eased speech; the author calls the genitive Layka reading weak, noting other passages agree on al-Ayka.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو علي سقوط ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The people reportedly had seven towns, and Shuʿayb was not one of them; he was from Midian, which is why he is called their brother elsewhere.
rows.anchor: وكانت مدن القوم سبعة فيما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The prophets' repeated invocation uses the same wording because the faith they call people to is one and the same.
rows.anchor: وجاءت الألفاظ في دعاء كل واحد من هؤلاء الأنبياء واحدة بعينها إذ كان الإيمان المدعو إليه معنى واحدا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question ألا تتقون is a gentle, tactful appeal.
rows.anchor: وفي قولهم عليهم السلام ألا تتقون عرض رقيق وتلطف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Beyond disbelief, their named offense was cheating the scales and diminishing people's property.
rows.anchor: وكانت معصيتهم المضافة إلى كفرهم بخس الموازين وتنقص أموال الناس بذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qistās is a properly balanced scale, an intensified form related to qist; Ibn ʿAbbas and Mujahid read it as conducting affairs by God's scale of justice.
rows.anchor: «القسطاس» المعتدل من الموازين وهو بناء مبالغة

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read qistās with a ḍamma on qāf; ʿIsa and the Kufans read it with kasra.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «بالقسطاس» بضم القاف من «القسطاس»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taʿthaw means to cause corruption, from the verb ʿathā, to corrupt.
rows.anchor: وتعثوا معناه تفسدون يقال عثا إذا أفسد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-jibilla means generations or the past creation.
rows.anchor: والجبلة القرون، والخليقة الماضية وقال الشاعر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses restates Shuʿayb's terms to make them secure, emphasizing that the condition concerned eight years of service.
rows.anchor: لما فرغ كلام شعيب قرره موسى عليه السلام وكرر معناه على جهة التوثق في أن الشرط إنما وقع في ثمان حجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ayyamā is an interrogative in the accusative governed by qaḍayta, with mā serving emphasis.
rows.anchor: وأيما استفهام نصبه ب قضيت وما صلة للتأكيد

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan reads ayyimā with a silent yāʾ; Ibn Masʿud reads ayy al-ajalayni mā qaḍayta.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الحسن «أيما» بسكون الياء، وقرأ ابن مسعود

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads ʿudwān with kasra on ʿayn, while the majority use ḍamma; the phrase means no liability against me in word or deed.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «فلا عدوان» بضم العين وقرأ أبو حيوة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wakīl means a witness who stands over a matter or takes charge of it.
rows.anchor: و «الوكيل» الشاهد القائم بالأمر، قال ابن زيد

rows.speaker: ابن زيد
rows.claim: After the marriage, Shuʿayb sent Moses to a house with staffs; Adam's staff repeatedly sprang toward Moses, so Shuʿayb recognized his prophetic designation and let him keep it.
rows.anchor: قال ابن زيد: ولما كمل هذا النكاح بينهما أمر شعيب موسى

rows.speaker: عكرمة
rows.claim: Ikrima says Gabriel gave Moses his staff at night as Moses was setting out for Midian.
rows.anchor: وقال عكرمة: إن عصا موسى إنما دفعها إليه جبريل ليلا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير
rows.claim: Asked which term Moses fulfilled, Saʿid b. Jubayr consulted Ibn ʿAbbas, who said Moses fulfilled the fuller term, since God's Messenger always fulfilled his promise; the Christian questioner accepted this.
rows.anchor: فقال قضى أكملهما وأوفاهما إن رسول الله صلى الله عليه وسلم إذا قال وفى

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas also reports that the Prophet asked Gabriel, who said Moses fulfilled ten years.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم سأل في ذلك جبريل فأخبره أنه قضى عشر سنين

rows.speaker: مجاهد
rows.claim: Al-Tabari transmits from Mujahid that Moses served ten years plus another ten.
rows.anchor: وحكى الطبري عن مجاهد أنه قضى عشرا وعشرا بعدها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author calls the twenty-year report weak; Moses set out with his family for Egypt, his homeland and people, after sensing his prophetic selection.
rows.anchor: قال القاضي أبو محمد: وهذا ضعيف وفي قصص هذه الآية

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says a Friday night brought lost fire, an unlit flint, a lost road, and severe cold; the light Moses saw was from God blended into a tree.
rows.anchor: قال النقاش كانت ليلة جمعة فقدوا النار وأصلد الزند وضلوا الطريق واشتد عليهم الخصر

rows.speaker: وهب وقتادة وابن مسعود
rows.claim: They identify the tree respectively as oleander, hawthorn, or acacia; other reports name azarole or another species.
rows.anchor: قال وهب كانت عليقا وقال قتادة عوسجا.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānasa means sensed, here by sight; the same word occurs for perceiving maturity in 4:6, and Hassan's line illustrates the usage.
rows.anchor: و «آنس» معناه أحس والإحساس هنا بالبصر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-Ṭūr is a known mountain in Syria; ṭūr can mean any mountain, though some specify a mountain without vegetation.
rows.anchor: وكان هذا الأمر كله في جانب الطور وهو جبل معروف بالشام،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses hoped to find directions or news of the route, or a burning coal from a large piece of wood, not a flame, to warm themselves.
rows.anchor: فقال لأهله أقيموا فقد رأيت نارا لعلي آتيكم منها بخبر عن الطريق أين هو أو جذوة وهي القطعة من النار

rows.speaker: ابن مقبل
rows.claim: Ibn Muqbil's line is cited for a large, dense piece of fuel that does not burn weakly or with a fierce flame.
rows.anchor: ومن ذلك قول الشاعر [ابن مقبل] : [البسيط] باتت حواطب ليلى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author supposes the original sense of jadhwa is tree roots used as fuel in the desert, supported by al-Sulami's line about smoke from roots.
rows.anchor: وأحسب أن أصل «الجذوة» أصول الشجر وأهل البوادي

rows.speaker: حمزة والأعمش وعاصم
rows.claim: They give three dialect readings of jadhwa: kasra for most readers, ḍamma for Hamza and al-Aʿmash, and fatḥa for ʿAsim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «جذوة» بكسر الجيم، وقرأ حمزة والأعمش

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ṣalā means the heat of fire; taṣṭalūn derives from it with tāʾ changed to ṭāʾ.
rows.anchor: والصلى حر النار، وتصطلون تفتعلون منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses was forty when commissioned as a prophet; as he walked toward the divine light the green tree moved away, and then he was called.
rows.anchor: فلما أتى موسى عليه السلام ذلك الضوء الذي رآه وهو في تلك الليلة ابن أربعين سنة نبىء عليه السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Shāṭiʾ means the bank or edge of the valley.
rows.anchor: و «الشاطئ» والشط ضفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: These verses urge believers still in Mecca to emigrate: God's land is wide, and staying under unbelievers' persecution is wrong when worship is possible elsewhere.
rows.anchor: هذه الآيات نزلت في تحريض المؤمنين الذين كانوا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن جبير وعطاء ومجاهد
rows.claim: They say oppression and wrongdoing in a land make emigration to a just land obligatory; Malik also holds this view.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن جبير وعطاء ومجاهد: إن الأرض التي فيها

rows.speaker: مطرف بن الشخير
rows.claim: Mutarrif reads God's land as a promise that provision is ample throughout the earth.
rows.anchor: وقال مطرف بن الشخير قوله إن أرضي واسعة عدة بسعة الرزق في جميع الأرض

rows.speaker: نافع وابن كثير وعاصم وابن عامر
rows.claim: They read yā ʿibādi with fatḥa; Ibn ʿAmir also opens the yāʾ in arḍī, while Nafiʿ and ʿAsim keep it silent.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وعاصم وابن عامر «يا عبادي»

rows.speaker: أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read the yāʾ in yā ʿibādi as silent; the passage likewise reports a silent yāʾ in arḍī from Nafiʿ and ʿAsim.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو عمرو وحمزة والكسائي بسكونها، وكذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Fa-iyyāya is an object of an implied verb understood from faʿbudūn; its fronting emphasizes exclusive worship.
rows.anchor: فإياي منصوب بفعل مقدر يدل عليه الظاهر تقديره فإياي اعبدوا فاعبدون على الاهتمام أيضا في التقديم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The certainty of death and return diminishes worldly fears of emigration, such as dying or going hungry, and urges prompt obedience and migration to God.
rows.anchor: تحقير لأمر الدنيا ومخاوفها كأن بعض المؤمنين نظر في عاقبة تلحقه في خروجه من وطنه أنه يموت أو يجوع

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most read tarjiʿūn with second-person tāʾ; a yāʾ reading is reported from ʿAsim and Abu Hatim from Abu ʿAmr.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور «ترجعون» بالتاء من فوق، ورويت عن عاصم

rows.speaker: أبو حيوة
rows.claim: Abu Haywa reads kullu nafsin dhāʾiqatun al-mawta, with tanwīn on dhāʾiqa and accusative mawta.
rows.anchor: وقرأ أبو حيوة «كل نفس ذائقة» بالتنوين «الموت»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of Gardens encourages believers who act righteously; lanubawwiʾannahum means to settle them securely, and ghurafan is the second object.
rows.anchor: ثم وعد المؤمنين العاملين بسكنى الجنة تحريضا منه تعالى، وذكر الجزاء الذي ينالونه، وقرأ

rows.speaker: حمزة والكسائي
rows.claim: They read lanuthwiyannahum from athwā, meaning to make them dwell; this reading is also attributed to Ali, Ibn Masʿud, al-Rabiʿ b. Khuthaym, Ibn Waththab, and Talha.
rows.anchor: وقرأ حمزة والكسائي «لنثوينهم» من أثوى يثوي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Another reading doubles the thāʾ rather than using hamza, so ghurafan is accusative after dropping the preposition fī; Yaʿqub reads with yāʾ and Ibn ʿAmir has ḍamma vowels on ghuraf.
rows.anchor: وقرأها بعضهم «لنثوينهم» بفتح الثاء وتشديد الواو معدى بالتضعيف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Patience and reliance on God gather all good, including patience in obedience and restraint from desires.
rows.anchor: ثم وصفهم تعالى بالصبر والتوكل وهاتان جماع الخير كله أي الصبر على الطاعات وعن الشهوات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The verse describes the terror of Judgment: excuses will not help wrongdoers, nor will they be granted another chance to gain satisfaction.
rows.anchor: هذا إخبار عن هول يوم القيامة وشدة أحواله على الكفرة في أنهم لا ينفعهم الاعتذار ولا يعطون عتبى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yastaʿtabūn means yaʿtabūn; although the usual form suggests seeking something, that sense would spoil the meaning here.
rows.anchor: ويستعتبون بمعنى يعتبون كما تقال يملك ويستملك، والباب

rows.speaker: عاصم والأعمش
rows.claim: They read yanfaʿu with yāʾ; a line of poetry supports this kind of agreement between the verb and its subject.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم والأعمش «ينفع» بالياء كما قال تعالى

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God has given people every kind of example and clarified truth, yet they persist in disbelief and call the people of truth false; God has sealed the hearts of the ignorant, whose unbelief was decreed.
rows.anchor: ثم أخبر تعالى عن قسوة قلوبهم وعجرفة طباعهم في أنه ضرب لهم كل مثل وبين عليهم بيان الحق

rows.speaker: أبو عبيدة
rows.claim: Abu ʿUbayda explains ṭabaʿa by analogy with a sword that has rusted very heavily.
rows.anchor: وذهب أبو عبيدة إلى أنه من قولهم طبع السيف أي صدىء أشد صدأ

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Prophet is told to be patient, trust God's true promise, and remain unmoved by people who lack certainty or insight.
rows.anchor: ثم أمر نبيه بالصبر وقوى نفسه لتحقيق الوعد ونهاه عن الاهتزاز لكلامهم

rows.speaker: ابن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read yastaḥiqqannaka from istihqāq; the majority read yastakhiffannaka from istikhfāf, and the two readers also report a silent nūn in that form.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي إسحاق ويعقوب «يستحقنك» بحاء غير معجمة وقاف

rows.speaker: علي بن أبي طالب
rows.claim: While Ali prayed dawn prayer, a Kharijite shouted a verse accusing him of shirk; Ali recognized the insinuation and answered by reciting the command to be patient.
rows.anchor: وروي أن علي بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه كان في صلاة الفجر فناداه رجل من الخوارج بأعلى صوته

none: verse text and surah transition only

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman was granted wisdom meaning sound belief, religious understanding, and intelligence.
rows.anchor: لقمان رجل حكيم بحكمة الله تعالى وهي الصواب في المعتقدات والفقه في الدين والعقل

rows.speaker: عكرمة والشعبي
rows.claim: Ikrima and al-Shaʿbi say Luqman was a prophet, while Mujahid and others regard him only as a righteous servant.
rows.anchor: واختلف هل هو نبي مع ذلك أو رجل صالح فقط، فقال بنبوءته عكرمة والشعبي،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas reports the Prophet said Luqman was not a prophet but a reflective, certain servant loved by God and given wisdom; he chose well-being rather than rule, and served as a Nubian judge in Israel.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس: سمعت النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم يقول «لم يكن لقمان نبيا

rows.speaker: سعيد بن المسيب ومجاهد وابن عباس
rows.claim: They describe Luqman as a black Nubian with cleft feet and thick lips, and a judge among the Children of Israel.
rows.anchor: قاله سعيد بن المسيب ومجاهد وابن عباس، وقال له رجل كان قد رعى

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Asked what brought him to his evident rank, Luqman replied: truthful speech and silence about what does not concern him.
rows.anchor: قال: صدق الحديث والصمت عما لا يعني

rows.speaker: ابن المسيب
rows.claim: Ibn al-Musayyib says Luqman was among the Nubians of Egypt; Khalid b. al-Rabiʿ calls him a carpenter, while other reports call him a tailor or shepherd.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن المسيب: كان من سودان مصر من النوبة، وقال خالد بن الربيع:

rows.speaker: لقمان
rows.claim: Luqman's aphorism calls the worst person one who does not care if people see him doing wrong.
rows.anchor: قيل له وأي الناس شر؟

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: An ashkur may follow an omitted preposition or explain the preceding gift; Luqman's wisdom centered on gratitude, including worship and belief, and gratitude benefits the grateful person, while God is self-sufficient and worthy of praise.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: أن اشكر يجوز أن تكون أن في موضع نصب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ḥamīd means praiseworthy: God deserves praise by His essence and attributes, unaffected by people's ingratitude.
rows.anchor: والله تعالى غني عن الشكر فلا ينفعه شكر العباد حميد في نفسه فلا يضره كفر الكافرين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Idh qāla may mean remember when Luqman said it, or We granted him wisdom when he said it; the wording is shortened because the preceding context makes it clear.
rows.anchor: وقوله وإذ قال يحتمل أن يكون التقدير واذكر إذ قال

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman's son was named Tharan.
rows.anchor: واسم ابنه ثاران

rows.speaker: نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر عن عاصم
rows.claim: These readers double the yāʾ and give it kasra in the three occurrences of yā bunayya; Hafs and al-Mufaḍḍal from ʿAsim double it with fatḥa.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وأبو عمرو وابن عامر وحمزة والكسائي وأبو بكر

rows.speaker: ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير وقنبل
rows.claim: Ibn Abi Barra reports Ibn Kathir with a silent yāʾ in the first occurrence, kasra in the second, and fatḥa in the third; Qunbul reports silence in the first and third and kasra in the second.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي برة عن ابن كثير «يا بني» بسكون الياء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning that shirk is grave injustice may be Luqman's own speech or a divine statement attached to it; the report about 6:82 supports the latter and says it calmed the Companions' alarm.
rows.anchor: وظاهر قوله إن الشرك لظلم عظيم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Companions' concern could be eased if the phrase were God's own statement; it could also be eased by God quoting a servant already described as wise and sound.
rows.anchor: وإنما يسكن إشفاقهم بأن يكون ذلك خبرا من الله تعالى، وقد يسكن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two verses interrupt Luqman's counsel; al-Tabari assigns them to Luqman's intended speech, but the author finds this unlikely because they concern Saʿd, and understands a return to Luqman's speech after the aside.
rows.anchor: هاتان الآيتان اعتراض أثناء وصية لقمان، ووجه الطبري ذلك بأنها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The instruction gives mother and father equal standing, then singles out the mother for pregnancy and nursing, yielding three shares of kindness for her and one for the father; the Prophetic answer names the mother three times, then the father.
rows.anchor: ثم خصص الأم بدرجة ذكر الحمل ودرجة ذكر الرضاع فتحصل للأم ثلاث مراتب وللأب واحدة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Wahnan ʿalā wahn can mean weakness upon weakness from pregnancy then childbirth, the weakness of child and mother, or steadily increasing weakness without specifying two episodes.
rows.anchor: وهنا على وهن معناه ضعفا على ضعف، وقيل إشارة

rows.speaker: عيسى الثقفي وأبو عمرو
rows.claim: They read wahn with fatḥa on the hāʾ; it has the same meaning as the majority reading with sukūn.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عيسى الثقفي «وهنا على وهن» بفتح الهاء، ورويت عن أبي عمرو

rows.speaker: الحسن وأبو رجاء والجحدري ويعقوب
rows.claim: They read wa-faṣluhu instead of wa-fiṣāluhu; the author says fiṣāl points to the counted duration of nursing by naming its endpoint.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور الناس «وفصاله» ، وقرأ الحسن وأبو رجاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jurists agree on two years as the nursing period for maintenance, but differ on milk kinship: exactly two years, two years plus connected days, or no effect after early weaning.
rows.anchor: والناس مجمعون على العامين في مدة الرضاع في باب الأحكام والنفقات، وأما

rows.speaker: سفيان بن عيينة
rows.claim: Sufyan says praying the five daily prayers thanks God, while praying for one's parents after them thanks one's parents.
rows.anchor: وقال سفيان بن عيينة من صلى الصلوات الخمس فقد شكر الله تعالى.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The clause ilaa al-maṣīr inserts a warning within the parental counsel.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: إلي المصير توعد أثناء الوصية

rows.speaker: سعد بن أبي وقاص والجماعة من المفسرين
rows.claim: The verses were revealed about Saʿd's mother, who vowed not to eat or drink until he left Islam; relatives forced liquid into her mouth, but she eventually relented when he remained firm.
rows.anchor: روي أن هاتين الآيتين نزلتا في شأن سعد بن أبي وقاص وذلك أن أمه حمنة بنت أبي سفيان

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The first verse commands kindness and respect, but parents are not obeyed in disbelief, major sins, or abandoning an individual duty; obedience is required in permissible matters, and leaving recommended acts for them is commendable.
rows.anchor: فمطلب الآية الأولى الأمر ببر الوالدين وتعظيمه، ثم حكم بأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Parents may be obeyed in collective jihad or by answering a mother during prayer when safe repetition is possible; concern for her safety may justify interrupting prayer, but this is not stronger than a recommendation.
rows.anchor: وتلزم طاعتهما في المباحات وتستحسن في ترك الطاعات الندب، ومنه أمر

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan disagrees: if a mother prevents her child from attending the night prayer out of concern, he should not obey her.
rows.anchor: وخالف الحسن في هذا الفصل فقال إن منعته أمه من شهود العشاء الآخرة شفقة فلا يطعها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kind companionship with unbelieving parents means supporting them financially and inviting them gently.
rows.anchor: وقوله وصاحبهما في الدنيا معروفا يعني الأبوين الكافرين أي صلهما بالمال وادعهما برفق

rows.speaker: أسماء بنت أبي بكر
rows.claim: Asma asked the Prophet whether to maintain a visiting maternal relative who desired connection; he said yes. Some understood her as rejecting Islam, but the author prefers that she wanted social support.
rows.anchor: ومنه قول أسماء بنت أبي بكر الصديق للنبي صلى الله عليه وسلم وقد قدمت عليها خالتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author thinks Asma's visitor wanted a relationship or support and came because she needed it; he identifies Asma's mother as Qutayla and Aisha's and Abd al-Rahman's mother as the early Muslim Umm Ruman.
rows.anchor: والأظهر عندي أنها راغبة في الصلة وما كانت لتقدم على أسماء لولا حاجتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Following the path of one who returns to God is a universal instruction to people; anāba means to turn back, and the path is that of prophets and righteous people.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: واتبع سبيل من أناب إلي، وصية لجميع العالم

rows.speaker: النقاش
rows.claim: Al-Naqqash says Saʿd was the addressee and Abu Bakr the one who returned to God; after Abu Bakr affirmed Islam, six companions accepted it, and verses 39:9 and 39:17-18 were revealed about them.
rows.anchor: وحكى النقاش أن المأمور سعد والذي أناب أبو بكر، وقال:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage concludes by warning of resurrection, return to God, recompense, and accounting for small and great deeds.
rows.anchor: ثم توعد عز وجل بالبعث من القبور والرجوع إليه للجزاء والتوقيف على صغير الأعمال وكبيرها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Luqman uses this example to teach his son the extent of God's power, using a mustard seed so tiny that human senses cannot weigh it, though God encompasses it in knowledge.
rows.anchor: المعنى وقال لقمان يا بني، وهذا القول من لقمان إنما قصد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The tiny measure may describe a physical object or a deed; the apparent sense is a hidden thing, supported by a report that the son asked about a seed lost in the ocean.
rows.anchor: وظاهر الآية أنه أراد شيئا من الأشياء خفيا قدر حبة، ويؤيد

rows.speaker: كثير من المفسرين
rows.claim: Many commentators take the mustard seed as sins and acts of obedience; this makes the admonition both hopeful and frightening, since nothing escapes God's bringing it forth.
rows.anchor: وذكر كثير من المفسرين أنه أراد الأعمال المعاصي والطاعات، ويؤيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the physical-object reading, the verse displays God's power but does not itself threaten or encourage reward.
rows.anchor: وفي القول الآخر ليس ترجية ولا تخويف

rows.speaker: عبد الكريم الجزري
rows.claim: He reads fatakun with kasra on kāf and a doubled nūn, from kann, a covered thing, supporting the concrete-object interpretation.
rows.anchor: ومما يؤيد قول من قال هي من الجواهر قراءة عبد الكريم الجزري «فتكن»

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read in tak with feminine tāʾ and mathqāla accusative as kāna's predicate, supplying an implied subject such as a matter, sin, or act of obedience.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء «إن تك» بالتاء من فوق «مثقال» بالنصب

rows.speaker: نافع
rows.claim: Nafiʿ alone reads mathqālu nominative, taking kāna as a complete verb; its feminine marker agrees with the feminine noun to which mathqāl is annexed, as the cited poetry illustrates.
rows.anchor: وقرأ نافع وحده بالتاء أيضا «مثقال» بالرفع على اسم «كان»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The cited poetic lines support the feminine verb form agreeing with a noun annexed to a feminine word.
rows.anchor: جهير الكلام جهير العطاس ... جهير الرواء جهير النعم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God forbids the cited traits associated with pre-Islamic arrogance and display.
rows.anchor: فنهى الله تعالى عن هذه الخلق الجاهلية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Sawt is a collective generic noun, explaining its singular form; Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads aswāt al-ḥamīr in the second phrase.
rows.anchor: وقوله لصوت الحمير أراد ب «الصوت» اسم الجنس

rows.speaker: ابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads ankar al-aṣwāt aṣwāt al-ḥamīr, pluralizing the second noun without the definite article.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة «أنكر الأصوات أصوات الحمير» بالجمع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Al-ghaḍḍ is restraining or lowering something's projection, such as the gaze, a camel's rein, or the voice.
rows.anchor: والغض رد طمحان الشيء كالنظر وزمام الناقة والصوت وغير ذلك

rows.speaker: ابن مسعود
rows.claim: Ibn Masʿud interprets the trust as financial deposits; another report from him extends it to all duties while treating financial trust as the greatest instance.
rows.anchor: فقال ابن مسعود هي أمانات المال كالودائع ونحوها،

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the trust as everything entrusted to a person, religious or worldly, including commands and prohibitions; the whole law is a trust.
rows.anchor: وذهبت فرقة، هي الجمهور، إلى أنه كل شيء يؤتمن الإنسان عليه

rows.speaker: أبي بن كعب
rows.claim: Ubayy b. Kaʿb includes a woman's chastity among the trusts.
rows.anchor: قال أبي بن كعب من الأمانة أن ائتمنت المرأة على فرجها

rows.speaker: أبو الدرداء
rows.claim: Abu al-Darda says ritual bathing after sexual impurity is a trust.
rows.anchor: وقال أبو الدرداء غسل الجنابة أمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The offer asked the great creatures to bear duties with reward for obedience and punishment for failure; they declined in fear, either through awareness God created in them or by addressing the angels within them.
rows.anchor: ومعنى الآية إنا عرضنا على هذه المخلوقات العظام أن تحمل الأوامر والنواهي وتقتضي الثواب إن أحسنت والعقاب إن أساءت

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the creatures asked to remain subject to God's will, obeying without being left to their own judgment or seeking reward.
rows.anchor: ويروى أنها قالت «رب ذرني مسخرة لما شئت أتيت طائعة فيه

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن جبير
rows.claim: They say the human accepted responsibility for the trust and was unjust to himself and ignorant of its magnitude.
rows.anchor: وحمل الإنسان الأمانة أي التزم القيام بحقها، وهو في ذلك ظلوم لنفسه

rows.speaker: الحسن
rows.claim: Al-Hasan interprets carrying the trust as betraying it and applies the verse to the unbeliever and hypocrite.
rows.anchor: وقال الحسن حملها معناه خان فيها والآية في الكافر والمنافق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The degree of blame among sinful believers varies according to their conduct.
rows.anchor: قال الفقيه الإمام القاضي: والعصاة على قدرهم

rows.speaker: ابن عباس والضحاك وغيره
rows.claim: They identify the human as Adam, who accepted the trust, was promised reward for good and punishment for evil, and disobeyed within the same day, losing Paradise.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس والضحاك وغيره الإنسان آدم تحمل الأمانة فما تم له يوم حتى عصى المعصية التي أخرجته من الجنة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس وابن مسعود
rows.claim: They also identify the human as Adam's son Cain, who had promised his father to guard the family while Adam traveled to Mecca.
rows.anchor: وقال ابن عباس وابن مسعود الإنسان ابن آدم قابيل الذي قتل أخاه وكان قد تحمل الأمانة لأبيه أن يحفظ الأهل بعده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some say al-insān means humankind generally; the author considers this apt because the trust itself is universal.
rows.anchor: وقال بعضهم الإنسان النوع كله وهذا حسن مع عموم الأمانة

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj explains that the creatures fulfilled their duties and declined the blame of disobedience, while humans accepted the blame attached to God's commands and law.
rows.anchor: وقال الزجاج معنى الآية إنا عرضنا الأمانة في نواهينا وأوامرنا على هذه المخلوقات

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On the majority interpretation, 41:11 describes a response to a direct command, while this verse describes refusal of an offered choice, so the passages are consistent.
rows.anchor: وتستقيم هذه الآية مع قوله تعالى: أتينا طائعين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the creatures refused the trust, but Adam accepted it between his ears and shoulders; God promised to protect his sight and modesty from the unlawful.
rows.anchor: وروي أن الله تعالى عرض الأمانة على هذه المخلوقات فأبت، فلما عرضها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The author omits further details of that report because they are not reliable.
rows.anchor: وفي هذا المعنى أشياء تركتها اختصارا لعدم صحتها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Some take the scene as metaphor: comparing the trust's burden with the creatures' capacity shows they could not bear it, as when one tests whether a beast can carry a load.
rows.anchor: وقال قوم: إن الآية من المجاز، أي إنا إذا قايسنا ثقل الأمانة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The lām in li-yuʿadhdhiba marks the outcome, since humans did not accept the trust in order to be punished; the outcome is punishment for hypocrites and polytheists and repentance for believers.
rows.anchor: وقوله ليعذب الله اللام لام العاقبة لأن الإنسان لم يحمل ليقع العذاب لكن حمل فصار الأمر وآل إلى أن يعذب

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority read wa-yatūba in the accusative conjoined to li-yuʿadhdhiba; al-Hasan b. Abi al-Hasan reads it nominative as a new clause.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور و «يتوب» بالنصب عطفا على قوله ليعذب

rows.speaker: ابن كثير ونافع وحمزة
rows.claim: These readers lighten the mīm in aman; the reading is also reported from the Meccans, al-Aʿmash, ʿIsa, Shayba, and al-Hasan, but al-Akhfash and Abu Hatim weaken it.
rows.anchor: وقرأ ابن كثير ونافع وحمزة: «أمن» بتخفيف الميم، وهي قراءة

rows.speaker: عاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي
rows.claim: They and several other readers use a doubled mīm, yielding the alternative am-man reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ عاصم وأبو عمرو وابن عامر والكسائي والحسن والأعرج وقتادة وأبو جعفر: «أمن»

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: For the light-mīm reading, the stronger interpretation is a rhetorical question comparing the night worshipper with the disbeliever who enjoys briefly before Hell; the context and the later question about knowledge support it.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: وهو الأظهر أن الألف تقرير واستفهام، وكأنه يقول: أهذا القانت

rows.speaker: امرؤ القيس
rows.claim: A line by Imruʾ al-Qays illustrates the rhetorical construction; on this reading the pause is after raḥmata rabbih.
rows.anchor: ونظيره قول الشاعر [امرئ القيس] : [الطويل] فأقسم لو شيء أتانا رسوله

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A second interpretation takes the opening alif as a vocative to a person with these qualities and asks whether such a person is equal; the author says it is sound but disconnected from the surrounding argument.
rows.anchor: والوجه الثاني: أن يكون الألف نداء، والخطاب لأهل هذه الأوصاف،

rows.speaker: أبو علي الفارسي
rows.claim: Abu ʿAli al-Farisi weakens the vocative interpretation; Makki says it is forbidden by Sibawayh, but the author disputes Makki's argument about the omitted vocative particle.
rows.anchor: وهذا معنى صحيح، إلا أنه أجنبي من معنى الآيات قبله وبعده،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: With the doubled mīm, am enters on man and requires comparison between two groups; the comparator can be understood before or after the clause, and the prior comparator is clearer.
rows.anchor: وأما القراءة بتشديد الميم فإنها: «أم» دخلت على: «من»

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas explains qānit as obedient; Ibn ʿUmar takes qnut here as Qurʾan recitation or prolonged standing in prayer.
rows.anchor: والقانت: المطيع، وبهذا فسر ابن عباس رضي الله عنه،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says whoever wants Judgment Day to be easy should let God see him praying or standing during the dark night; qnut can also mean supplication or silent worship.
rows.anchor: وروي عن ابن عباس أنه قال: من أحب أن يهون الله عليه الوقوف يوم القيامة،

rows.speaker: أبو سعيد الخدري
rows.claim: Abu Saʿid reports the Prophet defining qnut as obedience; Jabir reports that the best prayer is one with long qnut.
rows.anchor: وروى أبو سعيد الخدري عن النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم أن القنوت: الطاعة.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ānāʾ means hours; the singular can be anī, anā, or inī, with a Qurʾanic use in 33:53 and a Hudhayli poetic example for inī.
rows.anchor: والآناء: الساعات، واحدها: أني كمعى

rows.speaker: الضحاك
rows.claim: Al-Dahhak reads sajid and qāʾim in the nominative.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الضحاك: «ساجد وقائم» بالرفع فيهما.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Yaḥdhar al-ākhirah means being wary of its condition and terror; Saʿid b. Jubayr adds ʿadhāb, and ūlū means possessors, singular dhū.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: يحذر الآخرة معناه يحذر حالها وهولها. وقرأ سعيد بن جبير:

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: Most read yā ʿibādi with an open yāʾ; Abu ʿAmr, ʿAsim, and al-Aʿmash also read it silent, and several readers drop the yāʾ in connected reading.
rows.anchor: وقرأ جمهور القراء: «قل يا عبادي» بفتح الياء.

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says the verse was revealed about Jaʿfar b. Abi Talib and his companions when they planned to migrate to Abyssinia.
rows.anchor: ويروى أن هذه الآية نزلت في جعفر بن أبي طالب رضي الله عنه وأصحابه حين عزموا على الهجرة إلى أرض الحبشة

rows.speaker: مقاتل
rows.claim: Muqatil takes the good promised to those who do good in this world as a good reward in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: في الآخرة وهي الجنة والنعيم، قاله مقاتل

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi instead takes the promised good as an outcome, victory, or God's support in this world; the author prefers the Hereafter interpretation.
rows.anchor: قاله السدي. وكان قياس قوله أن يكون في هذه الدنيا متأخرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God's spacious earth means neighboring lands implied by the migration story; taking it as Paradise is an unsupported assertion.
rows.anchor: وأرض الله يريد بها البلاد المجاورة التي تقتضيها القصة التي في الكلام فيها،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The promise of reward without measure covers patience through hardship, emigration, support of the faith, and every act of obedience.
rows.anchor: ثم وعد تعالى على الصبر على المكاره والخروج عن الوطن ونصرة الدين وجميع الطاعات: بأن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: One interpretation says the patient receive their reward without being called to account for its pleasures or pursued for sins, identifying them with a Prophetic group who enter Paradise without reckoning.
rows.anchor: أحدهما: أن الصابر يوفى أجره ثم لا يحاسب عن نعيم ولا يتابع بذنوب،

rows.speaker: النبي
rows.claim: The hadith identifies seventy thousand from the Prophet's community who enter Paradise without reckoning as those who avoid omens, cauterization, and seeking incantations, and rely on God.
rows.anchor: هم الذين لا يتطيرون ولا يكتوون ولا يسترقون وعلى ربهم يتوكلون

rows.speaker: الجمهور
rows.claim: The majority take the phrase to mean the patient are paid without limit or enumeration, a metaphor for uncountable abundance; Qatada says there is no measure or scale.
rows.anchor: والمعنى الثاني: أن أجور الصابرين توفى بغير حصر ولا عد، بل جزافا،

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Qatada stresses that there is no measure or scale for the reward.
rows.anchor: حتى قال قتادة: ليس ثم والله مكيال ولا ميزان،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says that after 2:261, the Prophet prayed for more reward for his community; after 2:245 and then this verse, he said he was satisfied.
rows.anchor: وفي بعض الحديث أنه لما نزلت: والله يضاعف لمن يشاء

rows.speaker: الملائكة
rows.claim: The speakers of nahnu awliyāʾukum are angels who told believers not to fear or grieve; at death and the unveiling of truth they say they protected them in life and will be their allies in the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: المتكلم ب نحن أولياؤكم هم الملائكة القائلون: «لا تخافوا ولا تحزنوا»

rows.speaker: السدي
rows.claim: Al-Suddi says the angels guarded believers in worldly life and will be their allies in the next; fīhā refers to the Hereafter, tadʿūn means request, and nuzulan is a verbal noun.
rows.anchor: قال السدي المعنى: نحن حفظتكم في الدنيا وأولياؤكم في الآخرة

rows.speaker: الجمهور وأبو حيوة
rows.claim: The majority pronounce the wāw of nuzulan with ḍamma; Abu Haywa reads it with sukūn.
rows.anchor: وقراءة الجمهور: بضم الواو. وقرأ أبو حيوة: بإسكانها.

rows.speaker: الحسن ومقاتل وجماعة
rows.claim: They take the best-speaker verse generally: it includes anyone, past or present, who calls people to God and obedience and acts righteously.
rows.anchor: وإلى العموم ذهب الحسن ومقاتل وجماعة، وبين أن حالة محمد

rows.speaker: السدي وابن زيد وابن سيرين
rows.claim: They single out Muhammad's state as the especially prominent instance of the verse.
rows.anchor: ذهب السدي وابن زيد وابن سيرين

rows.speaker: قيس بن أبي حازم وعائشة وعكرمة
rows.claim: They say the verse was revealed about callers to prayer; Qays takes righteous action as prayer between the call and the commencement, and al-Naqqash reports this from Ibn ʿAbbas.
rows.anchor: وقال قيس بن أبي حازم وعائشة أم المؤمنين وعكرمة: نزلت هذه الآية

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Muezzins are included, but cannot be the exclusive revelation setting because the verse came in Mecca before the call to prayer existed there; broader calls to God, including jihad and restraining wrongdoers, are weightier, so the author prefers a general meaning.
rows.anchor: ومعنى القول بأنها في المؤذنين أنهم داخلون فيها، وأما نزولها فبمكة بلا خلاف ولم

rows.speaker: زيد بن علي
rows.claim: Zayd b. Ali says the call to God can be made by the sword.
rows.anchor: قال زيد بن علي المعنى: دعا إلى الله بالسيف

rows.speaker: الجمهور وابن أبي عبلة
rows.claim: The majority read innanī with two nūns; Ibn Abi ʿAbla reads innī with one.
rows.anchor: وقرأ الجمهور: «إنني» بنونين. وقرأ ابن أبي عبلة:

rows.speaker: فضيل بن رفيدة
rows.claim: Fudayl says that as a muezzin among Ibn Masʿud's companions, he was told by ʿAsim b. Hubayra to recite innanī mina al-muslimīn after completing the call, then cite the verse.
rows.anchor: وقال فضيل بن رفيدة: كنت مؤذنا في أصحاب ابن مسعود، فقال لي عاصم بن هبيرة:

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Good and evil are unequal; repeating wa-lā al-sayyiʾa emphasizes both directions of the comparison through ellipsis.
rows.anchor: فقرر أن الحسنة والسيئة لا تستوي، أي فالحسنة أفضل، وكرر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The command gathers noble manners: meet social friction with the best conduct, including greeting, courtesy, controlling anger, and generosity in paying and collecting.
rows.anchor: وقوله تعالى: ادفع بالتي هي أحسن آية جمعت مكارم الأخلاق وأنواع الحلم،

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn ʿAbbas says these virtues protect a believer from Satan and humble the enemy.
rows.anchor: قال ابن عباس: إذا فعل المؤمن هذه الفضائل عصمه الله من الشيطان

rows.speaker: مجاهد وعطاء
rows.claim: They explain the best response as greeting someone at a meeting; the author says greeting begins this wider practice but is only one part of it.
rows.anchor: وفسر مجاهد وعطاء هذه الآية بالسلام عند اللقاء، ولا شك أن السلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The simile says the enemy appears like a close friend, since a real enemy does not actually become one; his outward behavior only resembles a devoted friend.
rows.anchor: فدخل كاف التشبيه لأن الذي عنده عداوة لا يعود وليا حميما،

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ḥamīm is a close relative who cares for or protects a person; the pronoun in yulaqqāhā refers to the conduct implied by the command to respond best.
rows.anchor: والحميم: هو القريب الذي يحتم للإنسان. والضمير في قوله: يلقاها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The view that yulaqqāhā refers to the declaration lā ilāha illā Allāh is unsupported by the wording.
rows.anchor: وقالت فرقة: المراد: وما يلقى لا إله إلا الله، وهذا تفسير

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The praise of patience is comprehensive: patience in obedience and restraint from desires gathers the qualities of goodness.
rows.anchor: وذلك بين للمتأمل، لأن الصبر للطاعات وعن الشهوات جامع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A report says Abu Bakr endured an insult silently until anger overcame him and he replied; the Prophet said an angel had defended him until he answered, when the angel left and Satan came.
rows.anchor: وروي أن رجلا شتم أبا بكر الصديق بحضرة النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم فسكت أبو بكر ساعة

rows.speaker: قتادة
rows.claim: Ḥaẓẓ ʿaẓīm may mean great intelligence and merit, or a large share of Paradise and afterlife reward; Qatada chooses Paradise.
rows.anchor: والحظ العظيم: يحتمل أن يريد من العقل والفضل، فتكون الآية مدحا.
